title: feat: add Fal fallback for Z-Image
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds `fal-ai/z-image/turbo` as a fallback only after the Z-Image Vast pool fails with HTTP 503 or a network error.
- Keeps the public `zimage` model, aliases, Vast provider attribution, and $0.004/image customer price unchanged.
- Adds a hidden, paid-only internal Fal route and records Fal's $0.005/MP provider cost plus fallback attribution in Tinybird.
- Reuses the existing production `FAL_KEY`; no secret changes are included.

Validation:
- Live Fal probes at 512×512 and 1024×1024; the 1024×1024 request returned a valid JPEG in 1.33s.
- 21 focused fallback tests, 81 surrounding gen tests, and 332 registry/pricing tests pass.
- Gen typecheck and Biome checks pass.

Fal API reference: https://fal.ai/docs/model-api-reference/image-generation-api/z-image-turbo

gist.headline: Z-Image grew a spare wing
gist.blurb: When the Vast Z-Image pool is having a lie-down, Polli now quietly takes the Fal route instead. Same public model, same price, fewer interrupted pixel gardens.
gist.summary: Added fal-ai/z-image/turbo as an internal fallback for the public zimage model when the Vast pool returns HTTP 503 or a network error, while keeping aliases, Vast attribution, and the $0.004/image customer price unchanged.
gist.impact: Z-Image requests can now continue through Fal during Vast availability failures, with a verified 1024×1024 JPEG response in 1.33 seconds and no API or pricing changes for users.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Z-Image generation as a cozy image garden with two connected watering paths: the usual Vast path is briefly blocked by a harmless sleepy cloud marked 503, while Polli uses a small backup Fal water pipe to keep a bright image-flower blooming. Polli should wear a tiny mechanic tool belt, with a retro terminal showing a simple generated landscape; the fallback should feel seamless rather than alarming.
